digest.component_or_area: tracker initialization and environment identity management
propositions: Re-cloning the tracker without preserving git-ignored local state (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .ensure-applied) silently regenerates a new environment identity that invalidates all prior op-cert attestations.
The ensure-registry unit that mints .env-id checks only for file absence, never consulting event files to detect prior environment identities already written to the store.

When a store holds events stamped with env_id E1 but .env-id is absent, minting a new .env-id E2 leaves the store in an inconsistent state where existing attestations cannot be verified because the signing key from E1 is not recoverable.

Minting over a populated store with a different environment's events must emit a loud stderr warning naming the prior env id(s), the attestation consequence, and the four git-ignored files to carry over, while still completing to support multi-clone workflows.

The fsck command must detect and report ENV_ID_MISMATCH when the current environment's own author also wrote events under a different env_id, scoped by author to avoid false positives in healthy multi-clone topologies.
REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1 environment variable acknowledges a re-identification situation and quiets the warning to a single-line note while preserving a record of what was written over.
